latestPosts.caption:
I cried making this. There was a time I left home many years ago. When I was away in Tennessee (an absolutely beautiful place btw), I realized how much of home I missed… and how much of home I hadn’t yet explored. I cried a lot then, too. As someone who has always been an independent who loves to explore anywhere and everywhere, I couldn’t believe how emotional I was over PA, especially given how I couldn’t leave soon enough back in those days. I needed to spread my wings and I’m so glad I did. But I’m also so glad I eventually made my way back home and actually gave it the proper exploration it deserved. I hopped in my car to drive. My favorite activity. And I drove everywhere. No place was off limits. I moved to different regions of the Commonwealth and stayed there for extended periods of time. It opened my eyes up to so much. The differences in the people, the landscape, the energy. I felt like I was getting the best bargain deal of my life. All of this beauty… in one single state. How could I have been so blind and so lucky all at once? All that said, I vowed to never take home for granted again back when I was 19. And at 35, there’s still so much left to explore. 🙏🏼🥹 If you’re watching this from afar, I hope it provides you a sense of comfort. The feeling of home is one that can’t be perfectly replicated. I hope you find a little bit of peace and nostalgia here, wherever you are in the world. Home will always be here when you need it. 🫶🏼

#pennsylvania

latestPosts.caption:
Big news!! We’re moving back to Sarasota…into my childhood home! 

This house was thoughtfully and lovingly designed by my parents. It was built in 1989, nestled on five beautiful acres where I spent all 18 years of my childhood.

It’s where my three sisters and I rode dirt bikes, raised goats, built tree forts, swam for hours on end, and ran barefoot until the sun went down. Every inch of this place holds memories that shaped who I am.

After I left for college, my parents separated and both moved out. The house sat quietly and empty for years. It had since been rented, but my parents never had the heart to fully let it go. 

In the most generous and full-circle twist of fate, my dad has gifted this home to me and Ish—to breathe new life into it, to make it ours, and to start a whole new chapter of memories.

I can’t wait to renovate and make it our own, while preserving the spirit of what made this place so special. My mom poured her heart into this home and I can’t wait to do the same for our kids—to give them a childhood rooted in the same trees and trails that built mine. We have big plans and even bigger dreams for this property!

We’ll slowly begin the planning process now and start renovations in early 2026 before moving in. It will be a long road, but I hope you’ll stick around as we begin this journey. There’s so much in store, and I can’t wait to share every step with you. 

Here’s to coming home 💛

Cheers to new beginnings ✨ And thank you to @cityfurniture for the smoothest move ever🤍

This house holds so many beautiful memories for us. It’s where Sunday took her first steps and said her first words. We always knew it was temporary, but that doesn’t make it any easier to say goodbye. For the next few months, we’ll be living in the guest house of my childhood home while we renovate the main house. And if all goes as planned, this will be our last big move…ever 🥹

If you’re in Florida, @cityfurniture offers FREE moving with furniture purchases over $5k! They were incredibly professional, efficient, and so careful with everything we own. Truly could not recommend them more. 🥰

Help me design my guest/kids bathroom! 🚿 Cabinets are from @cabinetsdotcom, limestone pavers are from @zia_tile, and shower tiles are from @bedrosianstile 🤍

@bloomsupps #bloompartner

Primary bathroom design loading… 🤍🛁✨ 
Swipe to the original Tiffany pendant that inspired it all. This light hung in the kitchen of this very home. It is original to when my parents designed and built the home back in 1989. It’s one of the few original pieces I’m keeping, and now it gets a new chapter in our primary bathroom.

This light is setting the tone for the entire space…a vintage-inspired bathroom with a freestanding tub, timeless brass fixtures, a dreamy pink @bespokestudioinc zellige tile, and beautiful white craftsman @cabinetsdotcom cabinetry to tie it all together.

Blending old with new feels so personal to me. Keeping small glimpses of my childhood home as I remember it woven into this renovation is my way of honoring where I came from while creating something beautiful for our family now. 💖

latestPosts.caption:
My Portugal recap, what I did (and what I wore). A perfect trip planned by @tourlane! Don’t forget you can use code CAELYNN300 for $300 off your trip for a limited time!

Where we stayed:
Lisbon: Hotel Avenida Palace
Porto: Villa Foz Hotel

What we ate:
Lisbon: 
Quick bites: Copenhagen Coffee, Honest Greens
Standout dinner: Grano Pasta Fresco, this is not Portuguese food, but it was SO good 
Rooftop bar: Rossio 

Porto:
Breakfast: we ate breakfast at the hotel each morning
Lunch: we ate at loko and lapa lapa which were near the hotel, both were great and it was nice to enjoy the warmth and sunshine with an Aperol spritz. 
Dinner: terra, the fish in Portugal was amazing

What we did:
Lisbon:
We walked around a ton. We opted out for guided tours and decided to explore the city by foot the first few days. It was nice to ease into things and adapt to the jet lag
I loved Chiado there’s a lot to see and do in that area. 

Porto:
We headed to Miragaia to see the famous Igreja Do Carmia. I really wanted to go to Livaria Lello, but the line was pretty long. Next time! That area was beautiful and we walked around and shopped a bit.

The area we stayed in was right on the water so we saw the lighthouse, hung out by the ocean, enjoyed some great food, and thrift stores. 

My favorite thrift store in Lisbon was Refuse and my favorite one in Porto was Yeahllow 

I wanted a fun easy trip with my bestie, and this was exactly what we needed!
I’ve always been a sucker for anything with an open back 🕺🏼
